intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene on chromosome 10.

checks.claim: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 defect has been described in three patients from two families 6, 7 carrying three pathogenic variants in the PDSS1 gene, homozygous in one family and compound heterozygote in the other (Table 1).
checks.explanation: Homozygous and compound heterozygous PDSS1 variants are described.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 gene is located on chromosome 10.
checks.evidence_quote: identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1)
checks.explanation: The abstract places PDSS1 in a homozygous region of chromosome 10.

paragraphs.text: Primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency-2 (COQ10D2) is an autosomal recessive disorder of coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10) biosynthesis caused by mutation in PDSS1, which encodes prenyldiphosphate synthase subunit 1 (Mollet et al., 2007). The phenotype varies. Some patients have sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, with mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy (Nardecchia et al., 2021). Others have a severe, early-onset multisystem disorder with encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome or pulmonary hypertension, and death in early childhood (Nardecchia et al., 2021; Bellusci et al., 2021).

checks.claim: COQ10D2 is an autosomal recessive disorder of coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis caused by mutation in PDSS1.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified 2 novel inborn errors of CoQ10 biosynthesis in 2 distinct families.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes an inborn error of CoQ10 biosynthesis with a homozygous PDSS1 mutation, but it never states autosomal recessive inheritance or names the disorder COQ10D2.

checks.claim: PDSS1 encodes prenyldiphosphate synthase subunit 1.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1), which encodes the human ortholog of the yeast COQ1 gene
checks.explanation: The abstract names PDSS1 as prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1.

checks.claim: The COQ10D2 phenotype is variable.
checks.evidence_quote: PDSS1 deficiency is a clinically heterogenous rare disorder that deserves to be added to the differential diagnosis of optic atrophy associated with sensorineural deafness.

checks.claim: Some patients with COQ10D2 have sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, with mild intellectual disability, muscle weakness, and cardiac valvulopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: was characterized by neurosensorial deafness, optic atrophy, mild intellectual disability, muscular weakness, and cardiac involvement consisting in mild to moderate valvulopathy. Notably, in these cases, neurosensorial loss preceded optic atrophy, like in our cases.

checks.claim: Some patients with COQ10D2 have a severe early-onset multisystem disorder with encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome or pulmonary hypertension, and death in early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: with a much severe phenotype characterized by leukoencephalopathy with a lactic acid peak on spectroscopy, associated with a severe nephrotic syndrome that caused kidney failure and death at the age of 16 months.
checks.explanation: The paper supports the encephalopathy, nephrotic syndrome and early death. It does not mention pulmonary hypertension, which presumably comes from another source.

Nardecchia et al. (2021) noted that in these sibs, neurosensorial hearing loss preceded optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported 2 sisters born to consanguineous Egyptian parents. The older sister walked independently at 15 months but had severe language delay. At 4 years, profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss was found and treated with a prosthesis. She was later diagnosed with mild intellectual disability. Her visual acuity was reported as normal at 11 years. At 14 years she was referred for progressive visual loss, and her visual acuity was 1/10 bilaterally, with red-green dyschromatopsia. Fundus examination showed optic atrophy that was most marked in the inferior temporal sector. Visual-evoked potentials showed increased latency and reduced amplitude of the P100 waveform in both eyes. Optical coherence tomography showed bilateral reduction in retinal nerve fiber layer thickness. She also had diffuse mild muscle weakness and a mild postural tremor of the upper limbs. Brain MRI was normal. Echocardiography showed a moderately dysplastic mitral valve with moderate insufficiency, medium-grade tricuspid insufficiency with an estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 40 mmHg, and a moderately dilated left atrium. Her 6-year-old sister had bilateral sensorineural hearing loss and mild intellectual disability. At 6 years she developed decreased visual acuity, with optic atrophy and divergent strabismus. In both sisters, sensorineural deafness preceded optic atrophy.

paragraphs.text: Bellusci et al. (2021) reported a boy with primary CoQ10 deficiency due to biallelic PDSS1 mutations. He had been born prematurely after an in vitro fertilization pregnancy complicated by twin-twin transfusion. At 5 months he presented with failure to thrive, hypotonia, feeding difficulties, bilateral hearing impairment, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and distal phalangeal erythema. Laboratory studies showed anemia, lactic acidosis, 3-methylglutaconic and tricarboxylic aciduria, and decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes. He developed a progressive multisystem disorder with severe developmental delay, pyramidal dysfunction, seizures, tremor, optic atrophy, nystagmus, severe visual and hearing impairment, and chronic heart failure. Brain MRI showed mild cerebral atrophy at 12 months. At 24 months it showed cystic change in the white matter surrounding the lateral ventricles and in the commissural fibers, with small necrotic or porencephalic cysts. He died at 3 years of age. The authors suggested that the combination of phalangeal erythema, livedo reticularis, and pulmonary hypertension pointed to microvascular dysfunction.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency, Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous mutation in the PDSS1 gene (D308E). The mutation altered a conserved amino acid and was found by homozygosity mapping followed by sequencing. Mutant yeast COQ1 was introduced into a yeast strain lacking coq1, and the transformed yeast grew poorly on respiratory medium, indicating that the mutation caused the OXPHOS deficiency. Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change of this mutation as c.924T-G.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency, Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous asp308-to-glu (D308E) mutation in the PDSS1 gene, affecting a conserved amino acid. Mutant yeast COQ1 was introduced into a yeast strain lacking coq1, and the transformed yeast grew poorly on respiratory medium. Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change as c.924T-G.

checks.claim: Mollet et al. (2007) identified a homozygous D308E mutation in the PDSS1 gene in affected members of a family with CoQ10 deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: A genome-wide search for homozygosity in family 1 identified a region of chromosome 10 encompassing the gene prenyldiphosphate synthase, subunit 1 (PDSS1), which encodes the human ortholog of the yeast COQ1 gene, a key enzyme of CoQ10 synthesis. Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: The abstract reports a homozygous D308E change in PDSS1 in family 1, which has CoQ10 deficiency.

checks.claim: The PDSS1 D308E mutation affects a conserved amino acid.
checks.evidence_quote: Sequencing of PDSS1 identified a homozygous nucleotide substitution modifying a conserved amino acid of the protein (D308E).
checks.explanation: The abstract says the substitution changes a conserved amino acid.

checks.claim: Mollet et al. (2007) introduced mutant yeast COQ1 corresponding to PDSS1 D308E into a yeast strain lacking coq1.
checks.evidence_quote: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively, resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium
checks.explanation: Mutant yeast COQ1 was put into the yeast strain lacking coq1 (Deltacoq1).

checks.claim: Yeast lacking coq1 and transformed with mutant COQ1 corresponding to PDSS1 D308E grew poorly on respiratory medium.
checks.evidence_quote: Transformation of yeast Deltacoq1 and Deltacoq2 strains by mutant yeast COQ1 and mutant human COQ2 genes, respectively, resulted in defective growth on respiratory medium
checks.explanation: 'Defective growth on respiratory medium' means the same as growing poorly.

checks.claim: Nardecchia et al. (2021) gave the nucleotide change of the PDSS1 D308E mutation as c.924T-G.
checks.evidence_quote: c.924T> G (p.Asp308Glu) homozygous
checks.explanation: Table 1 gives the Mollet variant as c.924T>G (p.Asp308Glu), which is the same as c.924T-G (D308E).

paragraphs.text: In 2 sisters, born to consanguineous Egyptian parents, with sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, Nardecchia et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in the PDSS1 gene, resulting in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution at a highly conserved position. The variant was absent from gnomAD and lay within a 12-Mb region of homozygosity. Both parents were heterozygous for the variant. Of the unaffected sibs, 1 was homozygous wildtype and 1 was heterozygous.

checks.claim: Nardecchia et al. (2021) reported 2 sisters born to consanguineous Egyptian parents with sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Here we describe two young sisters with sensorineural deafness followed by optic atrophy, due to a novel homozygous pathogenic variant in PDSS1.
checks.explanation: The case description states the parents are consanguineous and Egyptian.

checks.claim: Using whole-exome sequencing, Nardecchia et al. (2021) identified a homozygous c.735G-T transversion in PDSS1, resulting in a gln245-to-his (Q245H) substitution, in the 2 sisters.
checks.evidence_quote: A whole‐exome sequencing analysis revealed a homozygous likely pathogenic missense variant c.735G > T in the PDSS1 gene, never reported in the public database GnomAD. This variant causes the amino acid change p.Gln245His

checks.claim: The PDSS1 Q245H substitution is at a highly conserved position.
checks.evidence_quote: in a highly conserved position (98.5%, Fig. 1A)

checks.claim: The PDSS1 c.735G-T variant was absent from gnomAD.
checks.evidence_quote: never reported in the public database GnomAD

checks.claim: The PDSS1 c.735G-T variant lay within a 12-Mb region of homozygosity in the sisters reported by Nardecchia et al. (2021).
checks.evidence_quote: The variant lies in a long region of homozygosity (12 Mb)

checks.claim: Both parents of the sisters reported by Nardecchia et al. (2021) were heterozygous for the PDSS1 c.735G-T variant.
checks.evidence_quote: its segregation was confirmed in her parents (I:1 and I:2)
checks.explanation: Segregation implies the parents are heterozygous carriers. The paper does not say heterozygous explicitly.

checks.claim: Of the unaffected sibs in the family reported by Nardecchia et al. (2021), 1 was homozygous wildtype and 1 was heterozygous for the PDSS1 c.735G-T variant.
checks.evidence_quote: the unaffected sister (II:2) and brother (II:3) was, respectively, homozygous wild‐type and heterozygous for the variant

paragraphs.text: In a boy with severe COQ10D2, Bellusci et al. (2021) identified biallelic mutations in the PDSS1 gene: a c.716T-G transversion resulting in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution, and a c.1183C-T transition resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution. The boy had mitochondrial encephalopathy, pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, distal phalangeal erythema, 3-methylglutaconic aciduria, and decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes. He died at age 3 years.

checks.claim: In a boy with severe COQ10D2, Bellusci et al. (2021) identified biallelic PDSS1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: a patient with primary coenzyme Q10 deficiency caused by biallelic mutations in the PDSS1 gene

checks.claim: One PDSS1 mutation in the boy reported by Bellusci et al. (2021) was a c.716T-G transversion resulting in a val239-to-gly (V239G) substitution.
The other PDSS1 mutation in the boy reported by Bellusci et al. (2021) was a c.1183C-T transition resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution.
The boy with biallelic PDSS1 V239G/R395X mutations had mitochondrial encephalopathy.
checks.evidence_quote: presented clinical features of mitochondrial encephalopathy associated with pulmonary hypertension

checks.claim: The boy with biallelic PDSS1 V239G/R395X mutations had pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis, and distal phalangeal erythema.
checks.evidence_quote: mitochondrial encephalopathy associated with pulmonary hypertension, livedo reticularis and particularly, chronic distal phalangeal erythema

checks.claim: The boy with biallelic PDSS1 V239G/R395X mutations had 3-methylglutaconic aciduria.
checks.evidence_quote: Laboratory testing showed elevated plasma lactate and 3-methyl-glutaconic and tricarboxylic aciduria.

checks.claim: The boy with biallelic PDSS1 V239G/R395X mutations had decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes.
checks.evidence_quote: decreased CoQ10 levels in lymphocytes

checks.claim: The boy with biallelic PDSS1 V239G/R395X mutations died at age 3 years.
checks.evidence_quote: the patient died at the age of 3 years old because of a progressive multisystem disorder

paragraphs.text: For discussion of the c.1183C-T transition in the PDSS1 gene, resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution, that was found in biallelic state in a patient with COQ10D2 by Bellusci et al. (2021), see PDSS1, VAL239GLY.

checks.claim: Bellusci et al. (2021) found the PDSS1 c.1183C-T transition, resulting in an arg395-to-ter (R395X) substitution, in biallelic state in a patient with COQ10D2.
checks.evidence_quote: biallelic PDSS1 mutations were identified (NM_014317.3: c.716 T > G (p.Val239Gly) and NM_014317.3: c.1183C > T (p.Arg395*))
checks.explanation: R395X found in biallelic (compound heterozygous) state with V239G.
